lemmas_for_the_keeper.note: No ladder node yet (provides = []). If T-lad-programme-properties makes the past boundary chart a node, this is its Minkowski entry, and minkowski_zero_not_pastBoundaryChart is its n = 0 non-entry. Nothing is proposed for programme/ladder.toml now.

findings: No finding about the paper. 2312.07443 is not ledgered and no statement of it is claimed here. The instance concerns ETT's programme predicate PastBoundaryChart (Causal/FlrwType.lean:120–155).

The predicate is inhabited: (minkowski n).PastBoundaryChart W Ũ 0 for n ≥ 1, W = {t > 0} (minkowski_pastBoundaryChart, MinkowskiPastBoundaryChart.lean:301). So not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType (Causal/FlrwType.lean:314) is not vacuous. This closes the gap raised in T-abs-flrw-type AUDIT-1 finding 1. FlrwType's SCOPE (:68–72), its main theorem's docstring (:311–313) and OQ-159's text ('no instance is built yet', registers/DECISIONS.md) now refer to a target that is done. They are not edited here: they are outside this dispatch.

Both (A) and (B) fail on W, each in the theorem's own shape (minkowski_posHalfSpace_not_flrwTypeA :380, minkowski_posHalfSpace_not_flrwTypeB :432). Every other hypothesis holds on W: T2, second countable, CausallyArcConnectedOn W, FutureOneConnectedOn W, ≤_W antisymmetric (minkowski_posHalfSpace_flrwType_check :447). So the theorem bites. The instance does not separate (A) from (B), however: it does not show that either is needed alone. (B) fails at every point x, not only somewhere: no I⁻(x, W) contains a Cauchy surface of W (:402).

n ≥ 1 is necessary: in ℝ^{1,0} no open set has a past boundary chart at any point (minkowski_zero_not_pastBoundaryChart :316). This is the static-spacetime analogue of timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart (Causal/FlrwType.lean:543). The evidence's 'n = 0 is excluded, as on the timelike line' is now a theorem.

Field (vi) as defined is weaker than Sbierski's (4.1) use (sbierski2023c.txt:1062–1072, :1137–1144). It asks only γ̃ 1 ≪_Ũ σ 1. The planned end point (9/10, x₀) satisfies it but does not lie in Sbierski's slab (19ε₀/20, ε₀) × (−ε₁, ε₁)^d with ε₀ = 1, since 9/10 < 19/20. This is a remark on the ETT reading, not a defect: the abstract proof uses only the relation.
questions: The dispatch lists '(B) if cheap' among 'the other hypotheses of the theorem that hold on W'. (B) does not hold on W; it fails at every point. I read the item as asking for (B)'s status, as the target's evidence does ('(A) or (B) fails for W, and both do'; '(B)'s failure is optional'). I proved ¬(B), and the stronger per-point form, not (B).

To show that the theorem needs (A) itself, or (B) itself, one would want an instance with a chart where exactly one of them fails. This instance has both failing. Is such a separating instance wanted, and in which model? Not attempted. In open subsets of Minkowski space (B) seems to fail generically, since a bounded I⁻(x, W) cannot hold an unbounded Cauchy surface. A separating witness probably needs a non-flat model (FLRW-like) or a compact spatial quotient.

OQ-159 (OPEN: are the six fields the notion of record?) is not decided. The instance proves all six fields, so it also proves each weakening the row names: p ∈ Ũ from (iv), (vi) at one compact set, (v)'s compactness only for (vi). If the author strengthens the chart instead, this module is where the stronger fields would be checked.

Ũ is a box (−1, 1) × B(0, 1/10), with a Euclidean ball in place of Sbierski's cube (−ε₁, ε₁)^d. The ETT predicate has no coordinates, so this is the dispatch's choice and changes nothing in the predicate.
kb_proposals: kb/0322 update: the past boundary chart is inhabited. Causal.minkowski_pastBoundaryChart (Causal.Model.MinkowskiPastBoundaryChart after graduation): ℝ^{1,n}, n ≥ 1, W = {t > 0}, Ũ = (−1, 1) × B(0, 1/10), p = 0, V = W ⊓ Ũ, γ̃(s) = (s/2, 0), s₀ = 1/4, σ(τ) = (9τ/10, x₀). (A) and (B) both fail there. ℝ^{1,0} has no chart (minkowski_zero_not_pastBoundaryChart).

In Minkowski space, a future-closedness field I⁺(x, Ũ) ⊆ I⁺(x, V) on convex Ũ, V is two applications of Causal.Flat.lt_iff_of_convex plus 'x ≪ y raises t'. No Cauchy data (Causal.BoundaryChartCauchy) is needed.

To make a Cauchy surface of an open W meet a vertical line τ ↦ (τ, y) of a static spacetime, use Causality.IsCauchySurfaceOn.exists_mem_connectedComponentIn (Causal.InextensiblePiece) with T = Prod.fst. The maximal piece never needs computing. Causal.InextensiblePiece is not in Causal.FlrwType's closure: import it.
